notes: The part between Routeburn Falls Hut and Lake Mackenzie Hut is above the bush line. Snow and avalanches are possible outside the summer season.
The two ends of the track are about 325 km apart by road. Arrange your transport before you go.
Camping is permitted only at Routeburn Flats and Lake Mackenzie.

routeburnflats.name: Routeburn Flats Hut and Campsite
routeburnflats.note: DOC hut and campsite. 15 tent sites. You must book before you go. Facilities: cooking, heating, mattresses, lighting, flush toilets. Boil the water before you drink it. It is 250 m from the track line on this map.

start.name: Routeburn Shelter
start.note: Start of the track, 25 km from Glenorchy. There is a shelter, toilets and a car park.

end.name: The Divide
end.note: End of the track on the Milford Road, 85 km from Te Anau. There is a shelter and toilets.

pois.name: Earland Falls
pois.text: Waterfall of 174 m beside the track. In heavy rain, use the flood track below it.

pois.name: Lake Harris
pois.text: Deep lake below Harris Saddle. The track goes along the bluffs above it.

pois.name: Key Summit
pois.text: A side track of about 1 hour there and back goes to small alpine lakes and a view of three valleys.

pois.name: Lake Howden
pois.text: A landslide destroyed Lake Howden Hut in February 2020. You cannot stay here.

pois.name: Harris Saddle / Tarahaka Whakatipu
pois.text: The highest point of the track, 1255 m, with a day shelter. A steep side track climbs Conical Hill: 1 to 2 hours there and back.

pois.name: The Divide Shelter
pois.text: Shelter from the Topo50 data. A place to rest out of the rain.
